edits.english: GEMARA: We learned in our Mishna that during wartime, soldiers do not have leisure, and there is no concern that they committed a transgression. And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this from that which is taught in another mishna (Ketubot 27a): With regard to a city that was conquered by an army laying siege, all the women married to priests located in the city are unfit and forbidden to their husbands, due to the concern that they were raped by the soldiers, even though it is wartime! Rav Mari resolved the contradiction and said: They do not have leisure to pour wine for libations, because they are concerned about the war, and the inclination for libation is not strong at that time. But they have leisure to engage in intercourse, because this inclination is strong, even during wartime.
Karkom - We translate it as a siege, karkomin.

edits.hebrew: כל כהנות - הנמצאות בתוכה פסולות לבעליהן, דאשת כהן אסורה אף באונס, אבל אשת ישראל לא. הא הכא דשעת מלחמה היא וקתני אסורות, דיש פנאי לבעול:

edits.english: All the women married to priests - Those found within it are disqualified from their husbands, for a priest's wife is forbidden even if raped, but an Israelite's wife is not. Here, it is wartime, and it teaches that they are forbidden, because there is leisure to engage in intercourse.
They do not have time to pour libations - Because the inclination for libation is not strong for them, and they are preoccupied with war.
They have time to engage in intercourse - Because their inclination is strong for them.

GEMARA: We learned in our Mishna that during wartime, soldiers do not have leisure, and there is no concern that they committed a transgression. And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this from what we learned in another Mishna: A city that was conquered by a karkom (an army laying siege to a city) — all the wives of priests within it are disqualified, as we are concerned that they may have been raped by the soldiers, even though it is wartime! Rav Mari said: They do not have leisure to pour libations, because they are concerned about the war, and the inclination for libation is not strong at that time. But they have leisure to engage in intercourse, because this inclination is strong, even during wartime.

The Tosafot asked: Perhaps it can be said that here the matter refers to after the war, when they have leisure! And they answered that the language of the Mishna is general, and implies whether the matter was during the war or after it. However, Rabbeinu Tam writes (in Sefer HaYashar) that the meaning of the Mishna there is specifically during wartime, to say that all the priestesses who were in the city at the time it was conquered are forbidden, even if they left there afterwards, as is also proven from the continuation of the Mishna there.

In Tractate Ketubot, there is another answer that was not brought here, which distinguishes between a karkom of the same kingdom and a karkom of another kingdom (and the matter was explained in opposite ways: some explained that a karkom of another kingdom fears that the enemy will come at any moment, and therefore has no leisure, which is not the case for a karkom of the same kingdom. Others explained the opposite, that the king of the same kingdom does not allow soldiers to break order, which is not the case for a karkom of another kingdom). Rabbeinu Tam wrote that it is the way of the Gemara, when bringing a topic from another place, to take only one answer that seems to them a better answer (Sefer HaYashar). However, the Ritv'a wrote that that answer did not relate at all to our Mishna, in which there is no difference what kind of karkom it was. And so, the Tosafot wrote there, but they explained that in our case, it is specifically a karkom of another kingdom.

edits.hebrew: ורמינהי עיר שכבשוה כרקום - וא"ת דלמא ההיא מיירי לאחר גמר המלחמה דאז יש להם פנאי? וי"ל דמשמע בכל ענין, אפי' קודם גמר המלחמה:

edits.english: And they raise a contradiction: A city that was conquered by a karkom - And if you ask: Perhaps that refers to after the war is over, when they have leisure? And it can be answered that it implies in any case, even before the war is over.
